Covers EDGAR's recent-filings index, which holds roughly the last 1000 filings; older history is not searched, and the respons

tools.description: The market-wide feed of filings as they land at the SEC, optionally filtered by form type. Built for monitoring agents that poll: the answer is cached for 60 seconds upstream, includes 8-K item codes so a watcher can filter on events, and every entry carries its accession number for pinning. Costs $

tools.name: filing_section
tools.description: Pull a single numbered item out of a 10-K or 10-Q as clean text: risk factors (1A), MD&A (7), business (1), and the rest. tools.name: compare_filings
tools.description: Year-over-year diff of a 10-K risk-factor or MD&A section: the added and removed passages plus a change ratio, so an agent gets what changed instead of two multi-megabyte filings to parse. Pass two accession numbers to pin exactly which filings are compared; otherwise the two most recent of that for

tools.name: verify_financial_claim
tools.description: Deterministic check of a numeric claim against the company's own XBRL as filed with the SEC. Returns supported, contradicted, or unverifiable, with the as-reported value and the accession number to cite. Costs $0.10 per call.

tools.name: filing_events
tools.description: A company's 8-K filings parsed into material events with decoded item codes: executive departures (5.02), restatements (4.02), acquisitions (2.01), cybersecurity incidents (1.05), and the rest. eventDate is when it happened, filedAt when it was disclosed. Costs $0.05 per call.

tools.name: company_financials
tools.description: Fetch an as-reported XBRL financial concept for a company across recent periods, each tied to the filing it came from. Note that many issuers report revenue under RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax rather than Revenues; if one returns nothing current, try the other. Costs $0.01 per

tools.name: who_holds
tools.description: Every 13F manager whose latest information table names the company: manager, CIK, filing date, accession number, plus the total count of reporting managers. The inverse of institutional_holdings; chain them to walk from a ticker to full parsed portfolios. Costs $0.05 per call.

tools.name: institutional_holdings
tools.description: An institutional manager's latest 13F-HR parsed and aggregated: top positions by value with shares, CUSIP, and share of portfolio. Works on managers (Berkshire, Bridgewater...), not operating companies. Pinned by accession number. Costs $0.05 per call.

tools.name: insider_trades
tools.description: A company's latest Form 4 filings parsed into data: who traded, their role, buy or sell, shares, price, and holdings after. The free EDGAR servers list Form 4s; this one reads them. Every filing pinned by accession number. Costs $0.05 per call.

tools.name: edgar_search
tools.description: Exact-phrase full-text search over every EDGAR filing since 2001. Returns the company, form, date, and accession number of each hit, ready to feed into filing_section or compare_filings. Costs $0.01 per call.

tools.name: activist_stakes
tools.description: The first public signal of an activist position: Schedule 13D and 13G beneficial-ownership filings naming a company over a window, newest first. A fresh 13D is where an activist campaign becomes public. Costs $0.05 per call.

tools.name: ipo_pipeline
tools.description: New S-1 and F-1 registration statements as they land at EDGAR, market-wide and newest first: the earliest public signal of a US IPO. Costs $0.01 per call.

tools.name: rewrite_ratio
tools.description: Mechanical rewrite ratio of a filing item year over year: added sentences divided by total sentences in the newer section, as a percent, with a magnitude band. This measures editing activity in the text, not risk and not exposure; a lightly reworded sentence counts as one removal plus one addition.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.signalnodus.ai" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: recent_filings, filing_section, edgar_search · Private data: recent_filings, filing_section, token_price, domain_report, cftc_positioning, token_report · Public sink: institutional_holdings, cftc_positioning · Destructive: filing_section, compare_filings, evm_balance, evm_gas, evm_receipt, token_price, fx_rate, domain_report, prediction_markets, government_contracts, lobbying, cftc_positioning, energy_data, crop_data, trade_flows, x402_audit, token_report, gas_optimizer.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: recent_filings, filing_section, edgar_search · Private data: recent_filings, filing_section, token_price, domain_report, cftc_positioning, token_report · Public sink: institutional_holdings, cftc_positioning · Destructive: filing_section, compare_filings, evm_balance, evm_gas, evm_receipt, token_price, fx_rate, domain_report, prediction_markets, government_contracts, lobbying, cftc_positioning, energy_data, crop_data, trade_flows, x402_audit, token_report, gas_optimizer

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
